title: Maximum Sum With Exactly K Elements
statement: You have an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, and a score that starts at 0. You must make exactly `k` moves. In one move you take any value `m` currently in `nums`, take it out of the array, put the value `m + 1` into the array in its place, and add `m` to your score. Return the largest score that `k` moves can produce.
notes:
## Intuition

A move never makes any value smaller, and it turns the chosen value into a bigger one. So the best first move takes the largest value `m`; that leaves `m + 1` in the array, which is now the largest, so the best second move takes it, and so on. The score is `m + (m + 1) + ... + (m + k - 1)`. Simulating the array and searching it for its maximum each move also works, at O(n·k).

## Approach

1. Scan `nums` once to find `largest`.
2. Repeat `k` times: add `largest` to `score`, then increase `largest` by one (the value just put back).
3. Return `score`. (The same total is `k * largest + k * (k - 1) / 2`.)

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, `k = 3`. The scan gives `largest = 5`. Move 0 adds 5 (`score = 5`, `largest = 6`), move 1 adds 6 (`score = 11`, `largest = 7`), move 2 adds 7 (`score = 18`). The answer is `18`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + k): one scan for the maximum and `k` cheap moves.
- Space: O(1): only a few numbers are kept.

## Pitfalls

- Taking different elements on different moves never helps; only the maximum matters, so no sorting is needed.
- The value put back is `m + 1`, so each later move earns one more than the previous one.
- Exactly `k` moves are made even when every value is equal; duplicates do not change the answer.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `largest` | the largest value currently in the array |
| `score` | the total collected so far |
| `move` | how many moves have been made |

narration.2: Start the search for the maximum below every possible value.
narration.4: Keep the biggest value seen so far.
narration.9: Take the current largest value and add it to the score.
narration.10: Its replacement is one bigger, so it is the largest for the next move.
narration.12: All k moves are made; return the total.
